items.definition:
to fill with horror; to shock
The news of the accident horrified everyone.

to make someone feel ashamed or foolish
He tried to humiliate her in front of her friends.

to become or make more intense
The storm began to intensify as it moved closer to the coast.

to be in the position of authority in a meeting or gathering
The judge will preside over the trial.

to feel or show great joy or delight
We all rejoiced at the good news.

to make or become unlikely to give way or overturn
The doctors tried to stabilize the patient's condition.

to use up; to reduce
We are depleting our natural resources rapidly.

to try hard to do or achieve something
We must endeavour to improve our services.

to assign the responsibility for something to someone
I wouldn't entrust him with such an important task.

to pay attention to; take notice of
You should heed the advice of your elders.

succeed in material terms; flourish financially
The business began to prosper after the new marketing campaign.

To tear or cut into small pieces
She shredded the documents before leaving.

To calm or relieve
She tried to soothe the crying baby.

To produce or generate
The new policy spawned a lot of debate.

to select, organize, and look after the items in a collection or exhibition
She curates a collection of contemporary art for the gallery.

to make (someone) ineligible for something
The athlete was disqualified for using banned substances.

to make or become more diverse or varied
Companies should diversify their investments to reduce risk.

to fill (someone) with great delight; charm
The beautiful music enchanted the audience.

to increase rapidly; to make or become more intense or serious
The dispute quickly escalated into a full-blown argument.

admit to a hospital for treatment
They had to hospitalize him after the accident.

cause (a person or part of the body) to become immobile
The accident left him partially paralyzed.

To retrieve or recover something previously lost, given, or paid
They worked to reclaim the land from the sea.

To fly or rise high in the air
The eagle began to soar above the mountains.

strengthen
They decided to fortify the castle walls against attack.

make a general statement
It's unfair to generalize about an entire group of people.

stay in a place longer than necessary
She liked to linger in bed on Sunday mornings.

feel or show sorrow for the death of (someone)
The family gathered to mourn their loss.

be or cause to be balanced or suspended
She poised herself on the edge of the diving board.

openly resist or refuse to obey
The small country continued to defy the larger nation's demands.

convert into a code
You should encrypt your data to protect it.

to have its main office or center in a particular place
The company decided to headquarter its operations in New York.

turn upside down or inside out
He inverted the glass to let it dry.

to lead wrongly
Don't let fear misguide your decisions.

compel or force (someone) to follow a particular course of action; restrict or limit
Budget limitations constrain our ability to expand.

to involve deeply; to submerge
She decided to immerse herself in her studies.

describe the distinctive nature or features of
His honesty characterises his approach to business.

make (something) denser or more concentrated; express (a speech or text) in fewer words
The fog began to condense into droplets on the leaves.

adapt a product or service to a particular country or region
We need to localize the software for the Japanese market.

make the best or most effective use of a situation or resource
We need to optimize our website for mobile users.

to cut the wool off a sheep or to cut something off cleanly
The farmer will shear the sheep next week.

to investigate or look around in a sneaky or prying way
Don't snoop through my personal belongings.

to check or prove the validity or accuracy of something
It's important to validate your parking ticket before leaving.

to murder (a prominent person)
The plot to assassinate the king was discovered.

to send someone away from a country or place as an official punishment
The king decided to banish the traitor from the kingdom.

(of a bright light) blind (a person or their eyes) temporarily
The bright stage lights dazzled the audience.

(of a person) cause (someone) to believe something that is not true, typically in order to gain some personal advantage
He tried to deceive his parents about his grades.

(of a volcano) become active and eject lava, ash, and gases; (of a conflict or dispute) break out suddenly and dramatically
The volcano is expected to erupt soon.

To escape or avoid.
He tried to evade capture by hiding in the crowd.

to put something in the wrong place and lose it temporarily
I always misplace my keys.

to renovate and redecorate
They plan to refurbish the old hotel.

set apart from the rest or from each other; isolate or divide
It's important to segregate waste for recycling.

to examine (a book, movie, etc.) officially and suppress unacceptable parts of it
The government decided to censor parts of the documentary.

to grant or bestow (a title, degree, benefit, or right) or to have discussions; exchange opinions
The university will confer degrees upon the graduating students next month.

convert into a coded form
The computer will encode the data for security.

remain in one place in the air
The hummingbird continued to hover near the flower.

write or carve words or symbols on something
They decided to inscribe a message on the monument.

protect from heat, cold, or noise by surrounding with material
We need to insulate the attic to save energy.

feel bitterness or indignation at (a circumstance, action, or person)
She resented his constant criticism.

involve (something) as a necessary or inevitable consequence.
The job will entail a lot of travel.

imagine as a future possibility
She began to envision a world without war.

create and perform spontaneously or without preparation
He had to improvise a speech on the spot.

(of insects or animals) be present in large numbers, typically so as to cause damage or disease
The old house was infested with mice.

to make less; to decrease
The new policy aims to lessen the impact of pollution.

to overcome, quieten, or bring under control
The police managed to subdue the suspect.
